title: Dorian
sound: Minor but bright; the natural 6th (F# in A) lifts it above the darker natural minor.
use: Minor vamps in funk, soul, Latin rock and modal jazz; m7, m6 and m9 chords, and the ii chord in a ii – V.
tip: Target F# over Am7: it is the 3rd of the D9, so landing on it as the chord changes makes the Dorian colour obvious.

title: Phrygian
sound: Dark and tense; the b2 (F in E) a half step above the root gives its Spanish, heavy-metal edge.
use: Metal riffs, film music and minor vamps where the bII chord moves to i.
tip: Trill between F and E on string 1 or 6, then rest on E; the half step down into the root is the Phrygian sound.

title: Lydian
sound: Major and floating; the #4 (G# in D) replaces the 4th, so nothing in the scale pulls away from the major chord.
use: Dreamy major vamps in rock instrumentals and film music; maj7, maj7#11 and add9 chords, and the IV chord in a major key.
tip: Land on G# over the E/D bar (it is the 3rd of E), then hold it over D: it sounds stable, not wrong.

title: Mixolydian
sound: Major with a bluesy, unresolved edge; the b7 (G in A) replaces the leading tone.
use: Rock, blues, folk and funk over dominant 7th chords and bVII – IV – I progressions.
tip: Target G as the chord changes to G, then bend or slide from G to A over the A chord to hear the b7 resolve home.

title: Aeolian (natural minor)
sound: Sad and serious; the b6 (F in A) gives it the darker colour that Dorian lacks.
use: Minor-key rock, pop and ballads; the i – bVII – bVI movement and m7 chords on the i.
tip: Over the F chord, lean on F and let it fall a half step to E as the progression returns to Am.

title: Locrian
sound: Unstable and dark; the b5 (F in B) means the tonic chord is diminished, and the b2 (C) adds tension.
use: Over m7b5 chords (the vii of a major key, the ii of a minor key) and in some metal riffs; rarely a home key.
tip: Play B then F in the low register so the tritone is clear, then step from C down to B to hear the b2.

title: Harmonic minor
sound: Minor with a raised 7th (G# in A), which leaves an exotic augmented 2nd between F and G#.
use: Minor-key cadences over V7 to i, classical and neoclassical metal, gypsy jazz and flamenco-tinged pop.
tip: Over E7 play G# and resolve it up to A as Am arrives; then play F to G# slowly to hear the augmented 2nd.

title: Melodic minor (jazz minor)
sound: Minor 3rd with a major 6th and 7th (F# and G# in A): minor at the bottom, major at the top, smooth and modern.
use: Jazz over m6 and mMaj7 tonic chords; also the parent of the altered, Lydian dominant and Locrian #2 scales.
tip: Over AmMaj7 target G# (the major 7th) and C (the b3) in one phrase; the pair defines the sound.

title: Phrygian dominant
sound: Phrygian with a major 3rd: the b2 (F in E) and the 3rd (G#) form an augmented 2nd with a Middle Eastern and flamenco colour.
use: Over the V7 chord in a minor key (E7 in A minor), flamenco, Middle Eastern, Jewish and Balkan music, and metal.
tip: Play F then G# then F, then resolve F down to E; over the F chord let F sound as the root, over E as the b9.

title: Dorian #4 (Ukrainian Dorian)
sound: Dorian with a raised 4th (D# in A), giving an augmented 2nd between C and D# and a crying, folk-like colour.
use: Klezmer, Eastern European and Balkan folk music; over m6 and m7 chords where a sharpened 4th is wanted.
tip: Play C, D#, E slowly and land on E; over the B7/A bar target D# as the 3rd of B7.

title: Lydian dominant
sound: Mixolydian with a raised 4th (G# in D): a bright dominant sound with a #11 instead of the clashing natural 4th.
use: Over 7#11 and 9#11 chords, non-resolving dominants, the bVII7 chord and tritone substitutes in jazz, funk and fusion.
tip: Hold G# against the D bass and compare it with G: G# floats, G wants to resolve. Target it as the 3rd of E/D.

title: Altered (Superlocrian)
sound: Root, 3rd and b7 plus every altered tension: b9, #9, b5 (#11) and #5 (b13). Maximum tension that resolves strongly.
use: Jazz and fusion over altered dominant 7th chords (7alt, 7#9, 7b9b13) resolving to the I or i chord.
tip: Over G7alt play Ab (b9) and resolve it down to G, the 5th of Cmaj7; or Eb (b13) down to E, the 3rd.

title: Locrian #2 (half-diminished)
sound: Locrian with a natural 2nd (C# in B), so the m7b5 chord gets a smooth natural 9 instead of the harsh b9.
use: Jazz over m7b5 chords, especially the ii in a minor ii – V; it sounds more modern than plain Locrian.
tip: Hold C# over Bm7b5 and then play C: C# is calm and modern, C is the darker Locrian sound.

title: Lydian augmented
sound: Lydian with a raised 5th (G# in C): the #4 and #5 together make a bright, suspended, unsettled major sound.
use: Jazz and film music over maj7#5 chords, such as the bIII chord of a melodic minor key (Cmaj7#5 in A minor).
tip: Target G# over Cmaj7#5 and compare it with G: the raised 5th is the note that makes the chord shimmer.

title: Mixolydian b6 (Aeolian dominant)
sound: A dominant scale with a minor 6th (C in E): the major 3rd is bright, the b6 is sad, so it sounds bittersweet.
use: Over a V7 chord that resolves to a minor chord (E7 to Am or AmMaj7), and in film and rock ballad writing.
tip: Over E play C and let it fall a half step to B; in the Am/E bar the same C becomes the 3rd of Am.

title: Major pentatonic
sound: Open and sweet; with no 4th or 7th it has no half steps, so every note sounds safe over the major chord.
use: Country, folk, rock and soul melodies and solos over major chords and major-key progressions.
tip: Make the 6th (E) your home note in licks over G; it gives the sweet country sound that the minor pentatonic cannot.

title: Minor pentatonic
sound: Strong and bluesy; five notes with no half steps, built around the b3 (C in A) and b7 (G).
use: The first soloing scale in rock and blues: over minor chords, minor-key progressions and dominant blues.
tip: Bend the 4th (D) up a whole step to E on string 3 and match the pitch by ear; then resolve to A on the downbeat.

title: Blues scale
sound: The minor pentatonic plus the b5 (Eb in A), a passing blue note that adds grit.
use: Blues, rock and jazz blues soloing over dominant 7th chords and minor vamps.
tip: Use Eb only in passing: slide from D through Eb to E, or hammer from Eb to E; do not rest on it.

title: Major blues
sound: The major pentatonic plus the b3 (G in E), which slides up into the major 3rd (G#).
use: Major-sounding blues, country, Southern rock and jump blues over dominant 7th chords.
tip: Hammer from G to G# on the I chord; the b3 to 3 move is the sound. Over A7 drop G# and use G, the b7 of A7.

title: Whole tone
sound: Six notes a whole step apart, with no half steps: dreamy and floating, with the #4 and #5 (F# and G# in C).
use: Over augmented triads and 7#5 or 9#5 dominant chords; impressionist and film music.
tip: Play the scale as a run up two octaves, then target G# over C7#5 and F# over C7b5.

title: Half-whole diminished (dominant diminished)
sound: Alternating half and whole steps from the root: b9, #9, #11 and a natural 13 (Ab, A#, C#, E in G) over a dominant 7th.
use: Jazz, fusion and blues over 7b9, 7#9 and 13b9 chords; any minor-3rd shift of a line keeps it in the scale.
tip: Play Ab, A#, B over G7 so the b9 and #9 resolve up to the 3rd; then move the same lick up three frets.

title: Whole-half diminished
sound: Alternating whole and half steps from the root: the diminished 7th chord plus a note a whole step above each chord tone.
use: Jazz over diminished 7th chords, including passing dim7 chords.
tip: Over Bdim7 play each chord tone with its upper neighbour (C# to B, E to D, G to F, A# to G#) and hear the chord sound through.

title: Bebop dominant
sound: Mixolydian plus a passing major 7th (F# in G), so a descending eighth-note line starting on a chord tone puts chord tones on the beats.
use: Bebop and swing lines over dominant 7th chords and the V7 (and its ii) in a ii – V.
tip: Start on G on beat 1 and run down the scale in eighth notes: G, F#, F, E, D, C, B, A; G, F, D and B fall on the beats.

title: Hungarian minor
sound: Harmonic minor with a raised 4th (D# in A): two augmented 2nds (C to D#, F to G#) give a dramatic, exotic sound.
use: Neoclassical and metal soloing, film music and Romantic piano music in the Hungarian style; over minor chords and mMaj7 chords.
tip: Play the run C, D#, E, F, G#, A in one position and hear both augmented 2nds; resolve D# up to E over the E chord.
